stella-case-study.question: What is Stella?
stella-case-study.answer: Stella is Zunkiree Labs' autonomous AI commerce agent. It handles the entire buying journey — product discovery, questions, objections, and checkout — without following a fixed script.

stella-case-study.question: How is Stella different from a normal chatbot?
stella-case-study.answer: A scripted chatbot can only handle expected questions and hands off or dead-ends on anything else. Stella is grounded in the merchant's product catalog and business rules, so it understands unscripted questions and can complete a purchase itself, including payment.

stella-case-study.question: Does Stella support Nepali payment methods?
stella-case-study.answer: Yes. Stella has native integration with eSewa, Khalti, and Fonepay for the Nepal market, alongside Stripe for international payments.

stella-case-study.question: Where can Stella be deployed?
stella-case-study.answer: Stella deploys on Daraz, Shopify, and WooCommerce today, with full API access for custom ecommerce platforms.

zenly-case-study.question: What is Zenly?
zenly-case-study.answer: Zenly is Zunkiree Labs' AI booking engine. It handles complex availability across providers, locations, and equipment, and resolves scheduling conflicts automatically.

zenly-case-study.question: How does Zenly resolve double-bookings?
zenly-case-study.answer: Zenly models availability as a constraint problem rather than a single calendar, so when a conflict comes up it proposes alternatives or automatically rebooks the affected appointment with the customer's approval.

zenly-case-study.question: How does Zenly reduce no-shows?
zenly-case-study.answer: It sends reminders timed to when a given customer is actually likely to respond, across SMS, email, or voice, and makes rescheduling easy so a change happens instead of a no-show.

zenly-case-study.question: What calendars does Zenly integrate with?
zenly-case-study.answer: Zenly syncs with Google Calendar, Outlook, and Apple Calendar, and can be embedded anywhere via a JavaScript SDK.

gaamma-case-study.question: What is Gaamma?
gaamma-case-study.answer: Gaamma is Zunkiree Labs' manufacturing ERP platform, unifying production planning, inventory management, and quality control with AI-driven predictive maintenance.

gaamma-case-study.question: How does Gaamma predict equipment failures?
gaamma-case-study.answer: Gaamma feeds real-time equipment monitoring data into a machine-learning model that flags likely failures before they happen, so maintenance can be scheduled instead of reacting to an unplanned stop.

gaamma-case-study.question: Does Gaamma require replacing our existing equipment or software?
gaamma-case-study.answer: No. Gaamma connects to PLCs, SCADA systems, IoT sensors, and accounting software already on the floor through standard protocols, so there's no rip-and-replace.

gaamma-case-study.question: What kinds of manufacturing does Gaamma support?
gaamma-case-study.answer: Gaamma is built for discrete manufacturing, process manufacturing, job shop production, and warehouse and distribution operations.

semantic-search-vs-keyword-search.question: What is the difference between semantic search and keyword search?
semantic-search-vs-keyword-search.answer: Keyword search matches the literal terms in a query against an index and ranks results by term frequency and rarity. Semantic search converts the query and documents into vector embeddings and retrieves by meaning, so it can match a query to a document that expresses the same idea in entirely different words.

semantic-search-vs-keyword-search.question: Is semantic search always better than keyword search?
semantic-search-vs-keyword-search.answer: No. Keyword search remains stronger for exact matches such as part numbers, error codes, and proper names, and it is cheaper to run and easier to explain. Semantic search is stronger for paraphrase and intent. Most production systems use both together rather than choosing one.

semantic-search-vs-keyword-search.question: What is hybrid search?
semantic-search-vs-keyword-search.answer: Hybrid search runs keyword and semantic retrieval together and combines the two rankings, often using a fusion method such as reciprocal rank fusion. It keeps exact matching for identifiers while adding semantic coverage for natural-language queries.

semantic-search-vs-keyword-search.question: Do I need to replace my existing search to adopt semantic search?
semantic-search-vs-keyword-search.answer: Not usually. A staged migration is the common path: keep the existing keyword index in place, add semantic retrieval alongside it, and combine the results. This whitepaper covers migration strategies for adding semantic retrieval to an existing product.

semantic-search-vs-keyword-search.question: How should I benchmark the two approaches?
semantic-search-vs-keyword-search.answer: Benchmark against your own corpus and real user queries rather than a public dataset, since relative performance depends heavily on your content and how users phrase questions. The whitepaper sets out how to construct a representative evaluation set and which metrics to track.

enterprise-ai-adoption-report.answer: It is written for enterprise technology leaders — CTOs, heads of engineering, and data and AI leads — who are planning or already running AI initiatives and want to compare their position against how other organisations are approaching the same decisions.

enterprise-ai-adoption-report.question: What does the adoption maturity model assess?
enterprise-ai-adoption-report.answer: It assesses readiness across data foundations, engineering capability, governance, and clarity of the business case, so an organisation can identify which constraint is actually limiting progress before committing budget.

enterprise-ai-adoption-report.question: Why do so many AI projects stall after the pilot stage?
enterprise-ai-adoption-report.answer: A prototype only has to work once, while a production system has to be correct repeatedly, monitored, owned by a team, and integrated with data that was never designed for it. The report examines the data-readiness, ownership, and success-criteria issues behind that gap.

enterprise-ai-adoption-report.question: Does the report cover budget and vendor selection?
enterprise-ai-adoption-report.answer: Yes. It includes budget allocation trends across AI initiatives and an analysis of the vendor landscape, alongside the maturity model and the authors’ outlook for where enterprise adoption moves next.

natural-language-processing-fundamentals.question: Do I need a machine learning background to use this guide?
natural-language-processing-fundamentals.answer: No. The guide explains embeddings, transformers, and fine-tuning in practical terms aimed at engineers building NLP systems rather than researchers. The goal is enough understanding to make sound architectural decisions.

natural-language-processing-fundamentals.question: What are embeddings and why do they matter?
natural-language-processing-fundamentals.answer: An embedding maps text to a vector of numbers positioned so that texts with similar meaning sit close together, which makes distance a usable measure of semantic similarity. This one idea underpins semantic search, clustering, classification, and retrieval-augmented generation.

natural-language-processing-fundamentals.question: When should I fine-tune a model instead of using it as-is?
natural-language-processing-fundamentals.answer: Fine-tuning is worth its cost when a task depends on domain language or output formats a general model handles poorly. In many cases careful prompting combined with retrieval performs comparably at lower cost, and the guide covers how to decide between full fine-tuning, parameter-efficient methods, and neither.

natural-language-processing-fundamentals.question: What does the guide cover about running NLP in production?
natural-language-processing-fundamentals.answer: It covers the operational concerns that determine whether a system survives real traffic: latency and throughput budgets, inference cost, model versioning, evaluation that catches regressions, and monitoring for drift.
